Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Summary of the game 1.1 GAME TURN 1.1.1 Farming 1.1.2 Expansion 1.1.3 Actions 1.1.4 End of turn 1.2 FLOOD 1.3 END OF GAME 1.4 WITH 2 PLAYERS Summary of the game GAME TURN Farming Sowing: the first player draws 5 Food cards twice and places them in order Harvest: in turn order, each player chooses one of the 2-card columns New turn order: depending on the columns that are chosen, a new turn order arises Expansion Each player, in turn order, performs all of the actions below. New huts: the player places a number of huts corresponding to the value of the Expansion of the current turn Resupplying: Using their cards, the player resupplies their huts Famine: unsupplied huts are removed from the board Wells: the player may place wells on the intersection of 3 hexagons on which they have huts. New wells earn 6/5/4 VP in 1st/2nd/3rd Reign. You can’t build a well next to a ziggurat. Wells can’t be placed between the two rivers. Wells can’t be placed on top of other wells. Building a well is not mandatory. A player may build several wells in the same turn. Once a well is built, it remains in place until the end of the game. The stock of wells is limited, so you cannot build more wells than what the stock contains. Earn Victory Points for villages and for constructed ziggurat levels: 1 VP if Above/Below River Hex 2 VP if Between River Hex 1 VP/Constructed Ziggurat Level Collect Camels (max 10 total): 3 for 1st hut on each river 2 per each additional river hut Actions Each player, in turn order, spends their camels (totally or in part) Build / extend a ziggurat (Cannot build on rivers or next to wells) Create intrigue in Assur Make an offering to the gods (Up to 3 camels) Buy a Plow or Food card (You may never hold more than 1 Plow card. Only 1 Food card may be bought each turn) End of turn If this is not the end of a Reign, place a new Expansion card. Otherwise, a Flood takes place. FLOOD Floods mark the end of a Reign. The first Reign ends after 2 game turns. The second and third Reigns end after 3 turns. Flooding: each hut located on the river is removed Assur: the players count their influence and score points depending on the Expansion cards of the current Reign (If tied, most huts wins. If still tied, higher hut wins) Dignitaries: the players score bonuses depending on the dignitaries on whose spaces they are placed (Higher: 1 to 8 points / Middle: a plow card / Lower: 1 camel per hut) Offerings: the players multiply their position on the offerings tracks with the number of ziggurats they own on the board Next reign : place the Bonus card (4-players); place a new Expansion card. END OF GAME At the end of the 3rd Reign, players score 1 point per ziggurat tile, 1 point per Plow card and 1 point for each group of 2 remaining camels. (In case of a tie for first place, all tied players share victory) WITH 2 PLAYERS Influence in Assur: the player with the most influence wins all points from Expansion cards. The second player wins nothing in the 1st Reign, and the value of the lowest card in the other 2 Reigns. [Rating: 2/10] This game offers almost no meaningful decisions. The turn order mechanic is coupled to random card draw and clearly broken, The theme is nonexistent. It is the worst game I have played in a long time, even worse than hermagor was. I am probably finished trying Mr Ornella's games.

[Rating: 2/10] I really, really don't like this game. I felt like I had negative control over what was happening. The constant teardown is fine, however the fact that it keeps you stuck in your corner and gives you basically no interaction is mind-numbing. There are so many mechanics that just happen and don't create an experience. Complexity for... what? What is the point? This is treading water in a pool staring across at your friends.

[Rating: 3/10] Oh No, (more lemmings)! Maybe it's a new definition of "entertainment", but I prefer to wash dishes than waste time on this time-vaccum, near-zero-decision, complex rules, repetitive ... game?

[Rating: 3/10] After 2 plays of this game, I think it's broken. After the 1st epoch, do whatever it takes to get into going first & stay going first, whatever other resources might look appealing, they won't be as beneficial as going first.

[Rating: 3/10] Unless I played it wrong, it just felt to constrictive to me.  I couldn't find a way to keep stuff on the board.  Even when you invest in, say - your site multiplier... it resets every round.  It didn't seem to matter what you "invested" in, it would just go away.  Most of your huts (which give you points and money [camels]) will just go away as you just can't keep them all fed.  I just don't enjoy super tight games like this where you end up "building" so little.  You don't lean back at the end, with yours hands interlocked behind your head admiring your vast empire... you just think "ok, so 

[Rating: 3/10] Dry as they come and elegance is nowhere to be found. I suppose people who claim to absolutely hate euros started off with this one... Uninteresting, boring and repetitive.   Looking at the board, I don't think all starting places are well balanced. I can also see a strategy to block a player from the game completely on the first turn.   Not my idea of a good game or a good time.

[Rating: 3/10] Having to constantly flick my eyes around the board to see which spaces have which symbols made this too much work to play again. My gut sense was that none of the mechanics was exciting either, though they were nicely varied.

[Rating: 3/10] 2024-04-16 - 3 - an old school eurogame, but it's not a good thing in this case. Assyria looked and felt old when it was published in 2009.  Assyria is repetitive with not so interesting actions and just boring. Also it's too long.

[Rating: 3/10] A lot of not much. If I'm buying, learning, setting up and playing something that's going to be over an hour, I want more than an unfulfilled promise of player interaction and a bunch of arbitrary point tracks to manage. Hurts itself further by looking like a contentious territory-control game that I might otherwise enjoy, making the reality even more of a letdown.  I might not even dislike it quite as much as my rating for it (I certainly don't enjoy it, though). But there's a meta-annoyance of what this game *almost* delivers that pulls it down further into frustration for me. I can name so 

[Rating: 4/10] I can see how this game would have its fans, but it's tough right now for this to distinguish itself from the legions of other similarly-themed euro games of this weight.  Ystari games have been becoming more and more mechanical and this one definitely has that type of feel - very dry, kind of soulless.    I'm not ready to write this one off yet though - there are definitely different viable strategies to pursue, so I will try to reevaluate after more plays, though it may be hard for me to find opponents.

[Rating: 4/10] Looks dull. Very unremarkable though there isn't anything particulary wrong with it. Excellent rules. Massive downtime problems. No way this plays in 45 minutes.

[Rating: 4/10] Lots of things happening in this game, and I can imagine people liking it. For me, however, the mechanics did not really come together, and neither did the theme.

[Rating: 4/10] This game was purchased mainly to be a 2 player game and for me it fell totally flat in that regard. I had high hopes for this one based on the idea that the board scaled to be smaller forcing the players to bump into each other more frequently. I just seems to me that while this happened the rest of the game needed to scale as well and it just didn't. It may be a better game with more players. Rating based solely on 2 player status.   [ImageID=554375]

[Rating: 4/10] Too many methods of scoring points, many of which seem to funnel players toward building ziggurats.

[Rating: 4/10] I'm probably suffering from Euro-fatigue, but this is a meaningless game of point mongering between options that are far from equally attractive. Forget any thoughts of building for the long term, this is strictly about maximising your score, now. The unforgiving food regime means that it's possible to enter a death spiral from the very beginning and that's completely unacceptable in a game of this length. I'm sure some will like it, but I'd rather play Austria in a Diplomacy tournament for psychopaths, than have to face this again.

[Rating: 4/10] The scoring in this game is way too convoluted and I think there are some game balance issues with the initial positions of the zigurats. In particular, two of them seem to be in inferior positions compared to the other two. Game also suffers from too much analysis paralysis.

[Rating: 4/10] Played once, felt flat. Now it's recently on BGA. I should try it once to confirm the score.

[Rating: 4/10] This was so exhaustingly boring. I'd rather not play this again. The game might have a brain but it has no heart.
